findings.summary: Acceptance verification is embedded in the live runner, preventing direct reuse of its provenance and publication checks.

assessment.reason: Maintainers cannot require or directly exercise the actual normalize, test-lifecycle and publication assertions without exiting through list mode or running a live model scenario. Changes to these high-consequence assertions therefore require reasoning through fixture/model orchestration, while offline suites exercise only lower-level helpers.
evidence: scripts/smoke_acceptance.rb:8-15 handles ARGV and exits or starts the live fixture at top level; requiring it is not a callable verification interface.
scripts/smoke_acceptance.rb:106-186 embeds normalize checkpoint/recovery, test A/B/C provenance and preservation assertions; lines 187-214 embed publication/readback/fixed-lease checks.
scripts/test_acceptance_support.rb and scripts/test_git_acceptance.rb require lower-level support modules rather than these actual driver assertions.
assessment.invariant: Extract only existing verification blocks behind explicit callable inputs while preserving their conditions, order, diagnostics, Git commands, approved-output mutations and current CLI/model/isolation behavior. Preserve all existing test scenarios/assertions; only scoped invariant guards may be added.

evidence: scripts/acceptance_support.rb now exposes verify_normalize!, verify_test_lifecycle! and verify_publication! with explicit keyword inputs; requiring support executes no client/workflow.

All three extracted verification bodies were compared by SHA-256 with their original driver blocks and are byte-for-byte identical. The driver retains CLI parsing, fixture/model setup, dispatch, guard ordering and the same 23 scenario names.

scripts/test_acceptance_oracles.rb directly exercises the actual extracted functions on synthetic inputs and owned temporary Git repositories: reviewed-prefix/private-proof rejection, independent recovery, approved-byte mutation, deferred/failed evidence, code-before-closure provenance, actual remote refs, paired readback, immutable expectations and missing-action leases.

Existing test bodies/assertions and live model/permission/budget behavior were preserved. Rake runs the new direct guards with the offline suite. No live model workflow scenarios were rerun; supplied unit traces do not certify workflow execution.

The runner appends workspace to reads at :81 after the instructions interpolated reads at :72.
assessment.invariant: Preserve check order, exact messages, warn side effects, the before and before_git snapshots taken before the model call and the final package-preservation check.

findings.summary: The acceptance scenario hash is an undocumented, untyped contract between acceptance_cases.rb, smoke_acceptance.rb and acceptance_support.rb, and prepare_history is a 97-line method with three boolean variants.

assessment.reason: A misspelt or renamed scenario key silently skips an oracle, related facts are held twice, and one variant overwrites six keys after construction, so each change needs reading all producers and consumers.
evidence: Producers: scripts/acceptance_cases.rb:24-115 and the prepare_* returns; consumers: about 30 scenario[:key] reads in scripts/smoke_acceptance.rb and scripts/acceptance_support.rb:163-285.
scripts/acceptance_cases.rb:192-193 sets expected_new_refs to nil while allowed_preparation_tracking is {} when unapproved; :331-338 overwrite six already-set keys when missing is true.
scripts/acceptance_cases.rb:248-344 is one method taking moved, discovery and missing flags.
assessment.invariant: Preserve key names and values and request text for every scenario, the side-effect order (hook written before registration, proof renamed only when missing is true) and raise messages.

findings.summary: The managed-rule marker line and expected rule-copy bytes are built by hand in seven places across three smoke and acceptance scripts.

assessment.reason: If adopt's marker format changes, someone must find seven sites, and these are paid-model scripts so a missed one is found late and expensively.
evidence: scripts/smoke_layout.rb:38-42 and :79-83, scripts/smoke_workflows.rb:51-56 and :90-97, and scripts/acceptance_cases.rb:16-18 each build '<!-- helm-rule: agent-helm@v<version> -->' plus the rule body.
The plugin version lookup from .claude-plugin/plugin.json is duplicated in smoke_layout.rb and smoke_workflows.rb.
assessment.invariant: Preserve the exact marker and body bytes, the 9.9.9 fixture version and the approved-output key order.

findings.summary: smoke_layout.rb and smoke_workflows.rb duplicate their fixture write, Claude and Codex command lines and answer parsing, and the two parsers have already diverged in wording.

assessment.reason: A pinned-model or tool-flag change needs two edits, and the parsing cannot be tested offline because it lives in load-time scripts.
evidence: scripts/smoke_layout.rb:90-96 and scripts/smoke_workflows.rb:104-110 repeat the Claude flags --setting-sources, --strict-mcp-config, --model, --effort and --tools.
scripts/smoke_layout.rb:110-119 and scripts/smoke_workflows.rb:114-125 parse modelUsage, is_error and result for Claude and agent_message events for Codex with different message wording.
scripts/smoke_workflows.rb:136-155 selects post-checks with eight if name == chains, and smoke_support.rb:31-45 dispatches preconditions on the names configuration-conflict and conflicting-config.
assessment.invariant: Preserve each script's timeout and process handling, the pinned CLAUDE_MODEL, every assertion and its message, and which cases run per client.

findings.summary: Several scripts contain provably dead code: duplicate checks that the validator already fails first, an unread scenario key, unused locals and unused requires.

assessment.reason: The shadowed checks suggest a second layer of protection that cannot fire, and the unused names add noise; grep shows no reflective or string-built use.
evidence: scripts/test_plugin.rb:18-22 and :29-31 repeat predicates that HelmValidation.validate raises for first (validate_plugin.rb:47, :49, :56, :59-61).
scripts/smoke_workflows.rb:55 sets rule_brand, which is read nowhere in scripts/.
scripts/acceptance_cases.rb:201 binds an unused left; scripts/test_git_acceptance.rb:72 binds an unused output.
Unused requires: scripts/smoke_layout.rb:2, :3 and :5, scripts/smoke_workflows.rb:3 and :4, scripts/test_smoke_support.rb:2; scripts/check_clients.rb:9 uses Pathname without requiring it.
assessment.invariant: Delete only the shadowed checks and unused names; keep the unique checks at test_plugin.rb:23-28 and :32 and every message the validator emits.

findings.summary: scripts/acceptance-plan.md states a model, a timeout and an extension target that no longer match the scripts or AGENTS.md.

assessment.reason: A reader following the plan would pin the wrong model for the older smoke scripts.
evidence: scripts/acceptance-plan.md:62 says Claude uses Sonnet 5.5 at high effort and item 2 says at most 240 seconds, while scripts/smoke_support.rb:7 pins claude-opus-5-5 and scripts/smoke_layout.rb:101 uses 300.
AGENTS.md says the first two smoke scripts pin Opus 5.5 and acceptance runs Sonnet 5.5.
scripts/acceptance-plan.md:45 says to extend smoke_workflows.rb, but the work landed in smoke_acceptance.rb.
assessment.invariant: Preserve the recorded design rationale; only scope the model and timeout statements to the scripts they describe.

findings.summary: The initial theme contract (storage key, modes, stylesheet naming, stylesheet id and error fallback) is written in both a Ruby heredoc in frontend.rb and in theme-switcher.js, and the fallbacks differ.

assessment.reason: A change to the key, a mode or the stylesheet naming must be made in a render-blocking inline script and a deferred file, and only the browser suite, which is not part of the offline test job, catches a mismatch.
evidence: docs/_plugins/frontend.rb:23-50 holds the inline bootstrap; docs/assets/js/theme-switcher.js:2-47 restates the agent-helm-theme key, system/light/dark modes, just-the-docs-{light,dark}.css names and helm-theme-stylesheet id.
The literals also appear in docs/scripts/browser_acceptance.py:12-13 and docs/tests/browser_frontend.mjs lines 44, 45, 64, 104, 105, 122, 142 and 157.
assessment.invariant: Preserve one stylesheet request, the render-blocking initial theme, behaviour with blocked storage, an invalid saved value, a failed dark stylesheet and cross-tab changes, the noscript default link and the #theme-mode selector.

findings.summary: The two guide-pair tests each discover pairs with their own glob and repeat the same assertions, and the glob walks docs/node_modules.

assessment.reason: Every run reads and parses front matter of about 155 third-party Markdown files, third-party front matter that fails YAML parsing could fail the tests, and a pairing-rule change needs two edits.
evidence: docs/tests/test_guide_views.rb:8-14 and docs/tests/test_human_guides.rb:16-20 both use root.glob('docs/**/*.md'); a find of docs/node_modules shows 155 Markdown files.
test_human_guides.rb filters only /_site/ and test_guide_views.rb filters nothing.
The overview_url computation, the overview match and the nav_exclude assertion appear in both files (test_guide_views.rb:19-21, test_human_guides.rb:28-30).
Both files also carry sibling-site branches (an agent-compass count and an unreachable elsif) whose intended parity is unconfirmed.
assessment.invariant: Preserve the pair count of 19, error messages, the no-paired-topics guard, and the split between the built-site test and the source test.

findings.summary: browser_frontend.mjs repeats its URL, context, background and diagram checks and keeps thirteen hand-written assertion tallies that nothing verifies.

assessment.reason: Adding or removing an assertion needs a manual tally edit, so the printed 'Passed N browser assertions' can drift silently, and a route or base-path change touches about thirteen literals.
evidence: docs/tests/browser_frontend.mjs lines 108-111 and 115-118 duplicate the background check, which is defined after its first inlined use, and lines 47 and 112 duplicate the diagram check.
assertions += tallies appear at lines 60, 68, 79, 89, 99, 113, 126, 137, 148, 160, 171, 181 and 222, and check-theme-colors.mjs:50 returns a constant 5.
The /agent-helm/docs/commands/... page literals repeat about thirteen times.
assessment.invariant: Preserve every assertion and message, selectors, the viewport and scheme matrix, the delayed-response fixtures and the PASS log lines.

findings.summary: Chrome discovery and the loopback static server with its origin restriction are implemented separately in render-diagrams.mjs and browser_frontend.mjs, with different platform coverage.

assessment.reason: A Linux or Windows machine with only Chromium can build the site but not run the browser tests, and the traversal guard and origin isolation are maintained twice.
evidence: docs/scripts/render-diagrams.mjs:7-19 tries HELM_DOCS_CHROME, macOS, /usr/bin/google-chrome, /usr/bin/chromium and Windows; docs/tests/browser_frontend.mjs:31 tries HELM_DOCS_CHROME, macOS and /usr/bin/google-chrome only.
The static server and the route.abort for other origins appear at render-diagrams.mjs:24-46 and browser_frontend.mjs:9-26.
AGENTS.md states only that Chrome must be installed and HELM_DOCS_CHROME overrides a nonstandard path.
assessment.invariant: Preserve the HELM_DOCS_CHROME override and error text, the loopback-only ephemeral listener, 404 and traversal behaviour, aborted off-origin requests and byte-identical diagram output.

findings.summary: docs/_config.yml has two defaults entries with the same scope that could be one.

assessment.reason: A reader must merge two identical-scope blocks mentally to see which front matter defaults apply.
evidence: docs/_config.yml:10-24 has two entries with path '' and type pages, one setting image and one setting layout.
assessment.invariant: Jekyll merges matching defaults in order, so the merged entry must produce the same image and layout for every page and keep the later title_category entries.
